tts.l-b2d00e6f.mp3: [cheerfully] Welcome to Victoria's Movie Night. Pick a question... and lights, camera, action!
tts.l-33e53fe4.mp3: [warmly] Welcome to Victoria's Movie Night! Tonight, our teams compete for glory... and for popcorn. Here is how it works.
tts.l-bc380aab.mp3: [warmly] Rules of the game. Pick a question from the board. [mischievously] Watch out for the plot twist... and for the popcorn bucket. [cheerfully] Play two rounds... and the Final Cut.
tts.l-964fe525.mp3: Pick a question. Five categories with five questions each. The higher the value, the harder the question. Teams take turns choosing a cell.
tts.l-7f45ca59.mp3: 30 seconds. The question is read aloud, then the clock starts. Only the team that picked it may answer. Everyone else stays quiet. Right: win the points. Wrong: lose them.
tts.l-a534233e.mp3: Play fair. No phones and no Googling. The host has the final word on close answers. Only one team steals the show.
tts.l-f6663818.mp3: [cheerfully] Ready? The first team, pick a question. Good luck... and may the best team steal the show! [laughs]
tts.l-4720d597.mp3: The sequel. Five new categories. Every value is doubled: 200 to 1,000. Same rules, bigger risks.
tts.l-5e6a63a1.mp3: The Final Cut. One final question. You see only the category first. Secretly wager up to half of your score. Low on points? You can always bet up to 500. You get 60 seconds. Right: add your wager. Wrong: lose it.
tts.l-7337aec3.mp3: [gasps] Plot twist! [mischievously] The team that found it... must give this question to another team.
tts.l-58cd94fa.mp3: [mischievously] So... who gets the plot twist?
tts.l-3a81092b.mp3: [excited] Let's dig into the popcorn bucket! [laughs] The first ticket picks the price. The second ticket picks the team that must answer. Answer right... and win it. Answer wrong... [whispers] and lose it.
tts.l-85b11123.mp3: [gasps] It's a tie! Time for a tiebreaker.
tts.l-083d607d.mp3: In 'Finding Nemo' (2003), what kind of fish is Nemo?
tts.l-9ff3dd12.mp3: The answer is: A clownfish. Real clownfish live among the stinging tentacles of sea anemones, which protect them.
tts.l-f28e7d08.mp3: What is the name of the friendly snowman in Disney's 'Frozen' (2013)?
tts.l-49af633e.mp3: The answer is: Olaf. He dreams of summer, not knowing what heat does to snow.
tts.l-93118e1a.mp3: In 'Toy Story' (1995), what is the name of the space ranger toy?
tts.l-d83dc90d.mp3: The answer is: Buzz Lightyear. 'Toy Story' was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.
tts.l-5fb90860.mp3: Which Japanese animated film by Hayao Miyazaki won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in 2003?
tts.l-78de9ce0.mp3: The answer is: Spirited Away. Miyazaki won the award again in 2024, for 'The Boy and the Heron'.
tts.l-a951e1f0.mp3: What was Walt Disney's first full-length animated feature film, released in 1937?
tts.l-45ddd31f.mp3: The answer is: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs. Many in Hollywood called it 'Disney's Folly' before it became a huge hit.
tts.l-a3cc03a7.mp3: The answer is: Peter Parker. He first appeared in a comic book in 1962.
tts.l-c10a6b60.mp3: The answer is: Gotham City. Bruce Wayne lives at Wayne Manor, with the Batcave hidden underneath.
tts.l-be8ed584.mp3: In 'Black Panther' (2018), what is the name of the hidden, high-tech African nation?
tts.l-5b1a2fbc.mp3: The answer is: Wakanda. Its technology is powered by a rare metal called vibranium.
tts.l-1213e339.mp3: Which unbreakable metal is bonded to Wolverine's skeleton?
tts.l-347b05d5.mp3: The answer is: Adamantium. Hugh Jackman played Wolverine in films for 17 years.
tts.l-737555c1.mp3: Which 2008 film, starring Robert Downey Jr., launched the Marvel Cinematic Universe?
tts.l-099bd9ac.mp3: The answer is: Iron Man. It ends with Tony Stark telling reporters, 'I am Iron Man.'
tts.l-fe197523.mp3: In 'Ratatouille' (2007), what kind of animal dreams of becoming a great chef in Paris?
tts.l-b1701371.mp3: The answer is: A rat. His name is Remy, and he cooks by steering a young man's hair from under his hat.
tts.l-e656ba5f.mp3: Which snack became a movie-theater favorite in the United States during the Great Depression of the 1930s?
tts.l-54219d3e.mp3: The answer is: Popcorn. It was cheap, filling and easy to sell, and it helped many theaters survive.
tts.l-dc29b58c.mp3: In 'Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory' (1971), what does Charlie find in his chocolate bar?
tts.l-7d1bcc96.mp3: The answer is: A golden ticket. Only five golden tickets were hidden in chocolate bars around the world.
tts.l-3fbad21a.mp3: In 'Forrest Gump' (1994), what does Forrest's mother say life is like?
tts.l-8e8f103c.mp3: The answer is: A box of chocolates. Because you never know what you're going to get.
tts.l-f43e48f2.mp3: In 'Breakfast at Tiffany's' (1961), what does Audrey Hepburn's character eat while looking into the jewelry store's window?
tts.l-9a92b306.mp3: The answer is: A pastry (a Danish) and coffee. The opening scene was filmed early in the morning on Fifth Avenue in New York.
tts.l-121906ba.mp3: Which film series is famous for the line 'May the Force be with you'?
tts.l-40d08e1f.mp3: The answer is: Star Wars. The first film came out in 1977.
tts.l-1960fd74.mp3: In 'The Wizard of Oz' (1939), who says 'There's no place like home'?
tts.l-f8048d9c.mp3: The answer is: Dorothy. She has to click the heels of her ruby slippers three times.
tts.l-9c52afeb.mp3: Which actor said 'I'll be back' in 'The Terminator' (1984)?
tts.l-e8e66a00.mp3: The answer is: Arnold Schwarzenegger. He went on to say versions of the line in many of his later films.
tts.l-f6fb1c8a.mp3: In 'Jaws' (1975), after seeing the shark, what does police chief Brody say they are going to need?
tts.l-22c53ed0.mp3: The answer is: A bigger boat. The line was improvised by actor Roy Scheider.
tts.l-a397b71c.mp3: Which 1972 crime film opens with the line 'I believe in America'?
tts.l-97692fd5.mp3: The answer is: The Godfather. It is said by the undertaker Bonasera, who has come to ask the Don for help.
tts.l-8eddb302.mp3: What is the name of the wizarding school in the 'Harry Potter' films?
tts.l-a0e14338.mp3: The answer is: Hogwarts. Students are sorted into four houses: Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw and Slytherin.
tts.l-4b4f5b78.mp3: Which secret agent is known by the code number 007?
tts.l-16cfd7c0.mp3: The answer is: James Bond. He was created by the British writer Ian Fleming in 1953.
tts.l-808fa2a7.mp3: In the 'Back to the Future' films, which car is turned into a time machine?
tts.l-12f9e752.mp3: The answer is: A DeLorean. It has to reach 88 miles per hour to travel through time.
tts.l-fce5a638.mp3: Which archaeologist adventurer, played by Harrison Ford, is afraid of snakes?
tts.l-f7b6c854.mp3: The answer is: Indiana Jones. His first adventure was 'Raiders of the Lost Ark' in 1981.
tts.l-b5fe1edd.mp3: Which 2003 film won all 11 Oscars it was nominated for, including Best Picture?
tts.l-eca83b64.mp3: The answer is: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King. It tied the record for the most Oscars won by a single film.
tts.l-d18972a4.mp3: Round Two. [mischievously] The stakes just went up.
tts.l-570d943c.mp3: What is the name of the hinged board snapped shut at the start of each shot?
tts.l-3db61050.mp3: The answer is: A clapperboard (slate). The snap helps editors match the sound to the picture.
tts.l-920e73c1.mp3: In filmmaking, what does 'CGI' stand for?
tts.l-e6d09615.mp3: The answer is: Computer-generated imagery. 'Jurassic Park' (1993) was a landmark for lifelike CGI creatures.
tts.l-b66b9ec4.mp3: What color is the screen most often used behind actors, so backgrounds can be added later?
tts.l-30596773.mp3: The answer is: Green. Green is used because it is a color rarely found in skin tones and most costumes.
tts.l-c0ffc74c.mp3: What job title is given to the person in charge of the camera and lighting, also called the cinematographer?
tts.l-2c79e67d.mp3: The answer is: Director of photography. On set, the role is often shortened to 'DP'.
tts.l-e5f8f393.mp3: Which 1927 film was the first feature-length 'talkie' with synchronized dialogue?
tts.l-38d2666f.mp3: The answer is: The Jazz Singer. Before it, feature films were silent, with live music in the theater.
tts.l-fa39ebc3.mp3: The answer is: Steven Spielberg. He is one of the most commercially successful directors in history.
tts.l-b411df63.mp3: Which director, known as the 'Master of Suspense', made 'Psycho' and 'The Birds'?
tts.l-20960e3a.mp3: The answer is: Alfred Hitchcock. He made brief cameo appearances in many of his own films.
tts.l-1242f9f4.mp3: Which Canadian director made both 'Titanic' and 'Avatar'?
tts.l-9f92db6e.mp3: The answer is: James Cameron. He was born in Kapuskasing, Ontario.
tts.l-87f2e662.mp3: Which New Zealand director brought 'The Lord of the Rings' to the screen?
tts.l-1c6c9449.mp3: The answer is: Peter Jackson. All three films were shot in New Zealand at the same time.
tts.l-9f22f274.mp3: Who became the first woman to win the Oscar for Best Director, in 2010, for 'The Hurt Locker'?
tts.l-2419dade.mp3: The answer is: Kathryn Bigelow. Only a handful of women have won the award since.
tts.l-864f07af.mp3: Which composer wrote the music for 'Star Wars', 'Jaws' and 'Indiana Jones'?
tts.l-54405c93.mp3: The answer is: John Williams. He has received more than 50 Oscar nominations, more than any other living person.
tts.l-82c4946b.mp3: In 'The Sound of Music' (1965), in which country does the von Trapp family live?
tts.l-206a75f4.mp3: The answer is: Austria. The film is based on the real von Trapp family singers.
tts.l-848b905e.mp3: Which 1977 film, starring John Travolta, made disco music a worldwide craze?
tts.l-716c0b19.mp3: The answer is: Saturday Night Fever. Its soundtrack, featuring the Bee Gees, became one of the best-selling albums ever.
tts.l-fdd809d5.mp3: Which 1994 Disney film features songs by Elton John and Tim Rice, including 'Circle of Life'?
tts.l-b6d60a37.mp3: The answer is: The Lion King. The story was later turned into one of the most successful Broadway musicals of all time.
tts.l-67bca083.mp3: Which Italian composer wrote the famous whistling theme for 'The Good, the Bad and the Ugly' (1966)?
tts.l-a886b2c3.mp3: The answer is: Ennio Morricone. He wrote music for more than 400 films and TV shows.
tts.l-ae1f391d.mp3: What famous sign stands in the hills above Los Angeles?
tts.l-1b5ebf38.mp3: The answer is: The Hollywood Sign. It first read 'Hollywoodland', as an advertisement for a housing development, in 1923.
tts.l-ff532c3d.mp3: What is the name of the famous Los Angeles sidewalk with stars honoring entertainers?
tts.l-5ab9cbc8.mp3: The answer is: The Hollywood Walk of Fame. It has more than 2,700 stars.
tts.l-b0519d5d.mp3: Which silent-film star was famous for his 'Little Tramp' character, with a bowler hat and a cane?
tts.l-1a52b9cc.mp3: The answer is: Charlie Chaplin. He was born in London in 1889.
tts.l-847b376b.mp3: Which 1939 film, set during the American Civil War, is often called the highest-earning film of all time when adjusted for inflation?
tts.l-e13a0366.mp3: The answer is: Gone with the Wind. Hattie McDaniel won an Oscar for it, the first ever won by a Black actor.
tts.l-00a597e9.mp3: In what year were the first Academy Awards held?
tts.l-01b4ac12.mp3: The answer is: 1929. The ceremony lasted about 15 minutes, and the winners had been announced three months earlier.
tts.l-8d9ccd88.mp3: Which Indian city's film industry is nicknamed 'Bollywood'?
tts.l-d9370ca2.mp3: The answer is: Mumbai. The name mixes 'Bombay', the city's former name, with 'Hollywood'.
tts.l-517aedf1.mp3: Which South Korean film won the Oscar for Best Picture in 2020, the first non-English-language film to do so?
tts.l-b9df2088.mp3: The answer is: Parasite. It was directed by Bong Joon-ho.
tts.l-b748765a.mp3: The film industry nicknamed 'Nollywood', one of the largest in the world by number of films, is in which country?
tts.l-84f97787.mp3: The answer is: Nigeria. It produces many hundreds of films every year, often on small budgets.
tts.l-1e93f80d.mp3: Which famous film festival is held every May on the French Riviera?
tts.l-e6cfb822.mp3: The answer is: The Cannes Film Festival. Its top prize is the Palme d'Or, or Golden Palm.
tts.l-8860ae19.mp3: Which French brothers held one of the first public film screenings for a paying audience, in Paris in 1895?
tts.l-df9b8ddd.mp3: The answer is: The Lumière brothers. Legend says that audiences ran from a film of a train pulling into a station.
tts.l-5a47cead.mp3: [whispers] It is time for the Final Cut. The final category is: Hollywood Legends. Write down your secret wagers. You may bet up to half of your score, or up to 500 if that is more.
tts.l-757021e3.mp3: Which actress holds the record for the most acting Oscars, with four wins for Best Actress?
tts.l-e1ae7821.mp3: The answer is: Katharine Hepburn. She won in 1934, 1968, 1969 and 1982.
tts.l-954e5fb6.mp3: In what year was the first 'Star Wars' film released?
tts.l-5a957839.mp3: The answer is: 1977. It was released in May 1977 and later retitled 'Episode IV – A New Hope'.
